elements.requirement: Except as provided by section 14 and section 15 of the Sale of Goods Act 1979 and subject to any other enactment, there is no implied term about the quality or fitness for any particular purpose of goods supplied under a contract of sale.
elements.quote: there is no implied term about the quality or fitness for any particular purpose of goods supplied under a contract of sale

elements.requirement: Where a seller sells goods in the course of a business, there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are of satisfactory quality.
elements.quote: Where the seller sells goods in the course of a business, there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are of satisfactory quality.

elements.requirement: Goods supplied under a contract of sale are of satisfactory quality for the purposes of the Act if they meet the standard that a reasonable person would regard as satisfactory, taking into account any description of the goods, the price if relevant, and all other relevant circumstances.
elements.quote: goods are of satisfactory quality if they meet the standard that a reasonable person would regard as satisfactory, taking account of any description of the goods, the price (if relevant) and all the other relevant circumstances

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, the quality of goods includes their state and condition.
elements.quote: the quality of goods includes their state and condition

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, fitness for all the purposes for which goods of the kind in question are commonly supplied is in appropriate cases an aspect of the quality of goods.
elements.quote: fitness for all the purposes for which goods of the kind in question are commonly supplied

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, appearance and finish are in appropriate cases aspects of the quality of goods.
elements.quote: appearance and finish

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, freedom from minor defects is in appropriate cases an aspect of the quality of goods.
elements.quote: freedom from minor defects

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, safety is in appropriate cases an aspect of the quality of goods.
elements.quote: safety

elements.requirement: For the purposes of the Act, durability is in appropriate cases an aspect of the quality of goods.
elements.quote: durability

elements.requirement: The implied term of satisfactory quality does not extend to any matter making the quality of goods unsatisfactory that is specifically drawn to the buyer's attention before the contract is made.
elements.quote: which is specifically drawn to the buyer’s attention before the contract is made

elements.requirement: The implied term of satisfactory quality does not extend to any matter making the quality of goods unsatisfactory which an examination ought to reveal, where the buyer examines the goods before the contract is made.
elements.quote: where the buyer examines the goods before the contract is made, which that examination ought to reveal

elements.requirement: In the case of a contract for sale by sample, the implied term of satisfactory quality does not extend to any matter making the quality of goods unsatisfactory which would have been apparent on a reasonable examination of the sample.
elements.quote: in the case of a contract for sale by sample, which would have been apparent on a reasonable examination of the sample

elements.requirement: Where a seller sells goods in the course of a business and the buyer makes known to the seller, expressly or by implication, any particular purpose for which the goods are being bought, there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are reasonably fit for that purpose (whether or not it is a purpose for which such goods are commonly supplied), except where the circumstances show that the buyer does not rely, or that it is unreasonable for the buyer to rely, on the skill or judgment of the seller.
elements.quote: there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are reasonably fit for that purpose, whether or not that is a purpose for which such goods are commonly supplied, except where the circumstances show that the buyer does not rely, or that it is unreasonable for him to rely, on the skill or judgment of the seller

elements.requirement: Where a seller sells goods in the course of a business, the purchase price or part of it is payable by instalments, the goods were previously sold by a credit-broker to the seller, and the buyer makes known to that credit-broker, expressly or by implication, any particular purpose for which the goods are being bought, there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are reasonably fit for that purpose (whether or not it is a purpose for which such goods are commonly supplied), except where the circumstances show that the buyer does not rely, or that it is unreasonable for the buyer to rely, on the skill or judgment of the credit-broker.
elements.quote: where the purchase price or part of it is payable by instalments and the goods were previously sold by a credit-broker to the seller, to that credit-broker, any particular purpose for which the goods are being bought, there is an implied term that the goods supplied under the contract are reasonably fit for that purpose

elements.requirement: An implied term about quality or fitness for a particular purpose may be annexed to a contract of sale by usage.
elements.quote: An implied term about quality or fitness for a particular purpose may be annexed to a contract of sale by usage.

elements.requirement: The provisions of section 14 apply to a sale by a person who, in the course of a business, acts as an agent for another as they apply to a sale by a principal in the course of a business.
elements.quote: apply to a sale by a person who in the course of a business is acting as agent for another as they apply to a sale by a principal in the course of a business

elements.requirement: The provisions of section 14 do not apply to an agent acting in the course of a business where the principal is not selling in the course of a business and either the buyer knows that fact or reasonable steps are taken to bring it to the notice of the buyer before the contract is made.
elements.quote: except where that other is not selling in the course of a business and either the buyer knows that fact or reasonable steps are taken to bring it to the notice of the buyer before the contract is made

elements.requirement: As regards England and Wales and Northern Ireland, the implied terms regarding satisfactory quality and fitness for a particular purpose under subsections (2) and (3) are conditions.
elements.quote: As regards England and Wales and Northern Ireland, the terms implied by subsections (2) and (3) above are conditions.

elements.requirement: Paragraph 5 of Schedule 1 of the Sale of Goods Act 1979 applies in relation to a contract made on or after 18 May 1973 and before the appointed day, and paragraph 6 applies in relation to a contract made before 18 May 1973.
elements.quote: Paragraph 5 of Schedule 1 below applies in relation to a contract made on or after 18 May 1973 and before the appointed day, and paragraph 6 in relation to one made before 18 May 1973.

elements.requirement: References to the appointed day in subsection (7) and paragraph 5 of Schedule 1 mean the day appointed for the purposes of those provisions by an order of the Secretary of State made by statutory instrument.
elements.quote: references to the appointed day are to the day appointed for the purposes of those provisions by an order of the Secretary of State made by statutory instrument

elements.requirement: Section 14 does not apply to a contract to which Chapter 2 of Part 1 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 applies.
elements.quote: This section does not apply to a contract to which Chapter 2 of Part 1 of the Consumer Rights Act 2015 applies
